review.mathematics: Write the five-digit palindrome as n=abcba=10001a+1010b+100c, where 1<=a<=9 and 0<=b,c<=9, so its digit sum is m=2a+2b+c. Since m is a two-digit square and m<=45, m is one of 16,25,36. Their digit sums are 7,7,9 respectively, and only 9 is a square, hence m=36. Because n is a square and ends in its nonzero leading digit a, checking square residues modulo 10 gives a in {1,4,5,6,9}. Also 2b+c<=27, so 36=2a+2b+c implies a>=5; therefore a is in {5,6,9}. Solving c=36-2a-2b with 0<=b,c<=9 gives exactly eight palindromes: 59895; 68886,69696; 95859,96669,97479,98289,99099. A square is congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 4, so the last two digits reject every candidate except 69696,96669,98289. Exact consecutive-square checks give 310^2=96100<96669<96721=311^2 and 313^2=97969<98289<98596=314^2, while 264^2=69696. Finally 6+9+6+9+6=36=6^2 and 3+6=9=3^2. Thus the unique pair is (m,n)=(36,69696). This derivation exhausts every allowed digit triple and does not assume that the modulo-4 condition is sufficient.
